proof:
# Two integer-centroid pieces cannot always both be locally Grünbaum-deep

This is an exact obstruction to strengthening the proved convex
partition theorem by requiring the true intrinsic centroid of EACH
piece to have continuous gamma_d-depth within that piece. It is not
an OC counterexample. Already n=d=q=1 suffices.

## 1. The actual body and the precise assertion excluded

Let

    C={ (z,x): 0≤z≤2, 0≤x≤z+1 },
    S=C intersect (Z times R),
    mu=H_1 restricted to S.

C is a compact full-dimensional convex trapezoid. Its three integer
fibers are exactly [0,1], [0,2], [0,3], of masses 1,2,3. Thus

    mu(S)=6,  integral_S z dmu=8.

Suppose C is covered by at most two positive-mass closed convex
subsets D_i⊆C, whose mixed overlaps are mu-null, and each true
intrinsic centroid has integer base. Then at least one centroid
has normalized depth at most 7/16 inside its own piece, strictly
below gamma_1=1/2.

In fact the proof needs only an almost-everywhere partition of S
by the two closed convex sets. It does not assume that the sets
have disjoint ambient interiors or are separated by one hyperplane.

## 2. All possible integer class means are forced

A single positive class would have base mean 8/6=4/3 and hence
would not qualify. For two positive classes their base means must
be distinct elements of {0,1,2}; if equal, the total mean would be
that same integer. The pair {0,1} cannot average to 4/3.

A class with base mean 0 is supported, up to mu-null sets, only
on the source fiber z=0: all base coordinates are nonnegative.
Likewise a class with base mean 2 is supported only on z=2.
Thus the pair {0,2} would leave the positive middle fiber uncovered.
The only possible pair of means is consequently {1,2}.

Let D be the piece with base centroid 1, E the other piece, and
let their masses be m_D,m_E. Conservation of mass and base moment
gives

    m_D+m_E=6,  m_D+2m_E=8,
    hence m_D=4, m_E=2.                              (1)

E has zero mass at z=0,1, so D contains the entire intervals there.
To justify “entire,” its traces are closed intervals and have full
measure in those source intervals; a closed proper interval cannot
omit a set of zero length only. Hence

    D_0=[0,1], D_1=[0,2].

Its z=2 trace I has length one. The z=2 trace J of E has length two.
Both are closed intervals in [0,3], their overlap has zero length,
and their union has full measure there and therefore is all [0,3].
There are precisely two possibilities:

    I=[0,1], J=[1,3],   or   I=[2,3], J=[0,2].        (2)

This classifies the mixed fiber traces that matter; no geometric
uniqueness of the ambient pieces between integer fibers is asserted.

## 3. The true centroids and their bad closed caps

In the first case of (2), the continuous moment of D is

    integral_0^1 x dx + integral_0^2 x dx
                        + integral_0^1 x dx =3.

Together with (1), its true centroid is y_D=(1,3/4). The closed cap

    H={x+4(z−1)≤3/4}

passes through y_D. On the three integer fibers it captures,
respectively, length 1, length 3/4, and zero. Thus

    mu(D intersect H)=7/4<2=gamma_1 mu(D).             (3)

In the second case the continuous moment is instead

    1/2+2+integral_2^3 x dx=5,

so the true centroid is y_D=(1,5/4). The closed cap

    H={x−4(z−1)≥5/4}

passes through this centroid and again captures lengths 1,3/4,0.
It therefore satisfies the same strict inequality (3). In both
cases all of the original-source mass in the displayed cap lies
in D; the other piece contributes zero cross-capture. The normalized
piece depth is at most `(7/4)/4=7/16`.

All cap boundaries and interval endpoints are included. Their
one-dimensional fiber measures at the boundaries are zero, so no
open-cap substitution or boundary-mass convention is used.

## 4. Both trace possibilities are geometrically realizable

The first case is realized by the actual closed halfspace partition

    D=C intersect {x+z≤3}, E=C intersect {x+z≥3}.

The second is realized by

    D=C intersect {x−2z≥−2}, E=C intersect {x−2z≤−2}.

Each displayed piece is a full-dimensional convex body, and each
pair covers ALL of C. Their common line has zero mixed measure.
The corresponding mixed traces are exactly (2), so the integer-
centroid partition theorem itself is unaffected and nonvacuous.

## 5. The original body satisfies OC with room to spare

The original point y=(1,1) has absolute mixed depth exactly 2 and
normalized depth 1/3. Here is an all-halfspace check. Every through-y
cap with positive x coefficient normalizes to

    x−1+a(z−1)≥0.

Its exact mass is

    F(a)=1+[-a]_0^1+[2+a]_0^3,
    [t]_0^b=max(0,min(b,t)).

Putting t=−a, the outer contribution is
`[t]_0^1+[2−t]_0^3`, which lies in [1,3] for all t:
it equals 3 for t≤−1, decreases from 3 to 2 on [−1,0],
equals 2 on [0,1], decreases from 2 to 1 on [1,2], and
equals 1 for t≥2. Hence 2≤F(a)≤4. The opposite cap orientation
has mass 6−F(a) because each nonvertical boundary is null, so it
also has mass at least 2. The bound 2 is attained, for example,
at a=−2 in the displayed orientation.

A through-y vertical cap captures either the z≤1 fibers, of mass
3, or the z≥1 fibers, of mass 5. A containing cap can be moved
through y without increasing mass. These observations cover every
closed ambient halfspace and establish the claimed depth.

The OC target here is gamma_1 M/2=3/2. Even the bad centroid caps
in (3) have original mass 7/4 above this target. The conclusion is
only that an exhaustive partition into at most 2^n true integer-
centroid convex pieces cannot universally make EVERY piece centroid
gamma_d-deep within its own mixed piece, even if one tries to use
outside-piece capture to repair these particular centroid caps.
